search_space: All 16 families G ⊆ P({0, 1}) were enumerated in increasing 4-bit mask order, with A fixed to P({0, 1}); for each family, σ(G) was computed to closure under ∅, Ω, complements, and binary unions.
witness_description: Take Ω = {0, 1}, A = P(Ω), and G = {{0}}. Then σ(G) = A but Ω is not an element of G.
refutation_explanation: Closing G = {{0}} under complements and finite unions produces ∅, {0}, {1}, and {0, 1}, so σ(G) = P(Ω) = A. Nevertheless, Ω = {0, 1} is not in G, refuting the assertion that being a generator also means Ω ∈ G.
